IMP with SLA for retraining can already outperform state-of the-art pruning during training algorithms without or with only small computational overhead and that only few epochs are needed to achieve most of its sparsity-vs.- performance trade-off.

, despite being a relatively simple algorithm, IMP can be considered an efficient, competitive and reliable approach for network compression.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

IMP with SLRe-training can be used as a competitive baseline for future work, that the global selection criterion is largely comparable to more complex approaches and finally, that only few epochs of retraining are actually needed in practice to get close to the optimal sparsity-vs.-accuracy trade-off of IMP.

IMP with SLRe for retraining can be considered a highly competitive and efficient baseline for network pruning.

IMP is a competitive and efficient approach for network pruning, and that it should be used as the default benchmark for future research.
